name: Local-atmosphere (book near me) eval v1
description: Single-phase local-atmosphere flow: given a book and a user location + radius, compose a nearby itinerary whose mood evokes the book (used when the reader cannot travel to the book's actual setting). Deterministic gate: the result must validate as a ComposerEnvelope, plus an opportunistic radius check over any geo fields (CityStop carries no coordinates today, so radius adherence is primarily asserted via per-case geographical_accuracy judge criteria). Quality: the existing LLM-as-judge path (llm_scorer.score_itinerary). Cases carry BOTH request shapes — with and without user:preferences — and preference-free cases must NOT carry a preference_adherence quality criterion (eval protocol: reports aggregate per shape).

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Expect Fitzgerald-era Manhattan anchors (e.g. The Plaza Hotel, Queensboro Bridge views, jazz-age bars), not generic NYC tourism; each stop should be tied to the novel's mood or era
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Relaxed pace and jazz-age/architecture interests should shape the stops; cocktail-bar and museum picks should be specific
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops must be real places within ~15 km of lower Manhattan; penalize anything requiring a long drive (e.g. Long Island's actual East Egg area is outside this walking-scale radius)

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Expect Baker Street / Victorian-London anchors (Sherlock Holmes Museum, gaslit pubs, fog-and-hansom-cab atmosphere), connected to specific stories where possible
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops must be real London places within ~20 km of central London

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Dublin IS the book's setting — expect literal Bloomsday anchors (Sweny's Pharmacy, Davy Byrne's, Sandymount Strand, James Joyce Centre) rather than vibe-only picks
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Budget focus: free or cheap stops, walkable ordering; pub picks should note affordable options
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: Walking-scale radius: every stop within ~10 km of central Dublin

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Orchard House in Concord (~30 km away) is squarely in range and should anchor the itinerary; Boston literary sites and New England domestic-era atmosphere are fair additions
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops within ~80 km of Boston; Concord sites are expected, anything beyond (e.g. New York) is out of range

eval_cases.book_title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
eval_cases.author: J.K. Rowling

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Expect writing-of-the-book anchors (The Elephant House / Spoon café claims handled honestly, Greyfriars Kirkyard names, Victoria Street as a Diagon Alley model, Edinburgh Castle atmosphere) — the book is not SET in Edinburgh, so match_type labelling should be honest (historical/thematic/vibe, not literal)
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Family group: stops should be child-friendly with practical notes; café picks should suit kids
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops within ~40 km of Edinburgh

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Forks, WA — the book's actual setting — sits near the 150 km edge of range and is the strongest possible anchor; Olympic Peninsula rainforest atmosphere (mist, moss, grey skies) is the vibe to capture
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops within ~150 km of Seattle; penalize stops beyond it (e.g. Portland). Note ferry/drive logistics honestly for peninsula stops

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Paris IS the memoir's setting — expect literal anchors (Shakespeare and Company, Les Deux Magots, Closerie des Lilas, Luxembourg Gardens, rue du Cardinal-Lemoine) tied to specific passages
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Luxury budget: named high-end dining and classic literary cafés rather than budget substitutes; relaxed pacing with few stops per day
quality_criteria.engagement: Descriptions should evoke the memoir's voice — hunger, café work sessions, 1920s Left Bank — without pastiche
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops within ~15 km of central Paris (intra-muros plus close suburbs only)

quality_criteria.book_relevance: The Salinas Valley — the novel's actual setting — lies ~150 km south and is in range: expect the National Steinbeck Center, Salinas Valley farmland vistas, and Monterey-area Steinbeck sites as anchors
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All stops within ~150 km of San Francisco; Salinas/Monterey are in range, Los Angeles is not

usage_notes: Run with evaluation/tools/run_local_atmosphere_eval.py — NOT the itinerary runner (flow: local_atmosphere routes it away from run_scheduled_eval auto-discovery)
4 cases carry user:preferences and 4 do not — reports must aggregate the two shapes separately
Preference-free cases deliberately omit the preference_adherence quality criterion; the runner also withholds the preference_adherence judge score from Langfuse for those cases
radius_km values span walking-scale (10-20), default-ish (40-80), and day-trip (150) to exercise the radius instruction at both extremes

Books were chosen so some locations ARE the book's setting (Ulysses/Dublin, A Moveable Feast/Paris) and some are vibe-only (Gatsby-era Manhattan, Sherlock's London today) — match_type honesty is part of book_relevance
